{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-ct-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"57d236b86b853c60e8b66f23d329624c1931140dace6300f80e2d908ed003f43","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-ct-class-d:lineage:37","source_registry_sha256":"07bbe76598f0084cdb2ee450c7050097675dacd13ccc4c40045c307297557e80","source_liveness_sha256":"8fea57e2daef73f0a94408791d2027c4fc2c9799e8d48060efecbf84d96aedf5"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Rules of the road","heading":"C — Rules of the road","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Rules of the road

FACT_ID: sec09-F01 | anchor: A38
Limits match road design, vehicle kinds and hidden driveways for perfect weather, so wet, blind or crowded miles demand slower wheels and can ticket even posted speeds. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0038]
FACT_ID: sec09-F02 | anchor: A38
Trust speedometers over gut feel, since drivers chronically undersense pace, worst dropping from expressways to local streets. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0038]
FACT_ID: sec09-F03 | anchor: A38
Stopping from sixty needs not double but triple plus the thirty mile per hour distance, so pace must fit sight and surface. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0038]
FACT_ID: sec09-F04 | anchor: A38
Crawling packs followers and forces risky passes, so pull aside for tailing queues or pick slower roads and quicker pace. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0038]
FACT_ID: sec09-F05 | anchor: A38
Panic stops betray blind eyes, invite skids and rear enders, so forecast trouble early, ease or sidestep, and halt fully at every sign and line. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0038]
FACT_ID: sec09-F06 | anchor: A38
Dry fifty costs four hundred reaction plus braking feet, a full block, and thirty costs two hundred, half a block, so shorter sight bans those speeds. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0038]
FACT_ID: sec09-F07 | anchor: A38
Law names who yields but grants no one passage, and every driver must still dodge people and cars at all costs. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0038]
FACT_ID: sec09-F08 | anchor: A38
Officer waves beat traffic lights, walkers in painted or implied crossings always win passage, and bike path crossings favor riders and walkers. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0038]
FACT_ID: sec09-F09 | anchor: A38
Cane and guide dog travelers hold absolute passage, and horns stay silent lest blasts confuse or scare them. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0038]
FACT_ID: sec09-F10 | anchor: A38
Left turners bow to straight oncoming traffic, and circle joiners bow to everyone already wheeling inside. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0038]
FACT_ID: sec09-F11 | anchor: A38
Unsigned corners yield to the right, and four way stops serve first arrivals first with right side ties. [A38]
Source: [A38 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0038]
FACT_ID: sec09-F12 | anchor: A39
Driveways, alleys and shoulders yield to main roads, boxes forbid entry without clear exits, passers yield even to slowing leaders, and signaling buses win merges. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0039]
FACT_ID: sec09-F13 | anchor: A39
Sirens, air horns and red or blue flashers order a right edge stop held through passage unless officers or firefighters wave on, clearing intersections first. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0039]
FACT_ID: sec09-F14 | anchor: A39
Flashing red school buses halt all directions and corners except oncoming traffic past medians or barriers, and release only past dark lights with children fully roadside and safety sure. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0039]
FACT_ID: sec09-F15 | anchor: A39
Trains crossing roads always take the right of way. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0039]
FACT_ID: sec09-F16 | anchor: A39
Roundabouts serve circulating traffic and crosswalk walkers first, guide multi lane entries by signs, exit on right signals past clear gaps, and never halt inside for joiners. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0039]
FACT_ID: sec09-F17 | anchor: A39
U-turns need sign checks and shun expressways outright, then run left signal, full stop, traffic scan, and opposite direction right lane entry. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0039]
FACT_ID: sec09-F18 | anchor: A39
Park off travel lanes in sight both ways, favor marked bays, brake plus gear or park, exit curbside after door checks, and pocket keys with locked doors. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0039]
FACT_ID: sec09-F19 | anchor: A39
Aim hill parked wheels hard roadside or curbside so runaways roll from traffic. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0039]
FACT_ID: sec09-F20 | anchor: A39
Never park in crossings, walks, blocking work zones, within twenty five feet of stop signs or safety zones, ten of hydrants, over a foot from curbs, across driveways or ramps, on bridges or tunnels, wrong sided, in handicap bays unpermitted, doubled, on rails, signed bans, or bike lanes. [A39]
Source: [A39 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0039]
FACT_ID: sec09-F21 | anchor: A40
Burn headlights to be seen, flash highs to announce, always pair wipers with lights by law, light early dusk, shun parking lamps rolling, and glow driving from low suns. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0040]
FACT_ID: sec09-F22 | anchor: A40
Run highs on empty dark stretches for double vision, dim near oncoming blocks, drop low behind cars and crowds, drop low in fog and storms with fog lamps, and never cruise parking lamps alone. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0040]
FACT_ID: sec09-F23 | anchor: A40
Answer stuck high beams with quick flashes, then hug the right edge if glare persists, and never duel brights since mutual blindness follows. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0040]
FACT_ID: sec09-F24 | anchor: A40
High beams reach four hundred feet capping speed near fifty, soupy storms shrink sight to two hundred feet ordering full pull offs, and blind hills and bends demand stop ready pacing. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0040]
FACT_ID: sec09-F25 | anchor: A40
Tap horns lightly for lane straying walkers and riders, merging passers and dozing drivers, but blast sharply for darting kids and elders, imminent strikes, and runaway cars. [A40]
Source: [A40 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0040]
